gaps.problem: Tokenwise C1 maps do not by themselves establish one numerically identical phenomenal occurrence across several token-relative experiential organizations.
gaps.counterexample: two tokenwise isomorphic codomains can be represented by distinct carrier copies unless a grounded comparison/quotient is additionally admitted
gaps.fixed: R185 claims coherent structural correspondence only and explicitly excludes numerical phenomenal identity and exclusive ownership.
gaps.open_premise: independently warranted cross-token phenomenal comparison or subject-individuation bridge

gaps.problem: No actual human, biological subsystem, prosthetic loop or artificial agent has been shown to realize the declared token carriers, complete signatures and shared occurrence.
gaps.counterexample: a supposed local token may be only a scientific view or may omit a constitutive boundary mechanism
gaps.fixed: Every membership conclusion is conditional on independently admitted actual tokens and faithful complete token-relative organization.
gaps.open_premise: same-episode actual bearer, interval, complete signatures and physical occurrence tracing

gaps.problem: Perturbation propagation distinguishes the finite models only if occurrence-specific isolation and synchronizer clamping are physically faithful.
gaps.counterexample: an unmodelled common driver or unclamped synchronizer makes distinct copies covary
gaps.fixed: Use and membership remain prior ontic claims; intervention is typed as evidence and the synchronizer is represented as an extra relation.
gaps.open_premise: actual path measurement and intervention isolation

gaps.problem: Incidence, quotient and gluing mathematics are established, and CG20261008 already contains the general coherent-overlap result.
gaps.counterexample: renaming coherent gluing as a new cross-scale theorem would duplicate existing work
gaps.fixed: R185 claims only the occurrence-sensitive membership application, incidence-count correction and synchronizer boundary as project-level increments.
gaps.open_premise: theorem-level external prior-art comparison before publication

gaps.problem: Occurrence membership does not yet explain which cross-scale relation supports action-centering, felt trying or familiar mineness.
gaps.counterexample: shared and copied architectures can match all declared reports and baseline outputs
gaps.fixed: No feeling label is attached to the incidence profile and the next question requires an independent selected relation or an underidentification proof.

gaps.problem: UCT-MAP-v1.0.0 completed a frozen 1,278-item semantic census, but R185 landed later and its delta plus affected dependents have not received a new completed semantic release audit.
gaps.counterexample: a structurally valid acyclic rule graph can still contain a false or scope-shifted rule
gaps.fixed: R185 remains a disabled PENDING_CHECKPOINT. Compatibility against the reconstructed v1.0.0 active graph is recorded separately and does not alter the completed release.
gaps.open_premise: new-version semantic review of the R185 delta and affected dependents, plus reviewer-controlled disposition

gaps.problem: The first R185 audit used the historical 584/284/178 root and named pre-release layers; a concurrent UCT-MAP-v1.0.0 release changed the authoritative effective-map boundary to 722 active nodes, 343 active rules and 203 context links.
gaps.counterexample: a clean audit against the unchanged root graph can still miss duplicate IDs or cycles against a newer effective overlay
gaps.fixed: The v1.0.0 capsule was hash-verified and reconstructed. R185 was retested as a disabled addition: 734 combined unique nodes, 348 active rules, 203 unchanged contexts, with no duplicates, unresolved references, empty all_of sets or cycle. Navigation now keeps v1.0.0 authoritative and labels R185 as a checkpoint.
gaps.open_premise: semantic integration in a new immutable release; structural compatibility is not semantic truth
